issue.title: Per-PDF unchanged-skip cache inside bob ref scan

task_type_fields.proposal:
Add a per-PDF unchanged-skip cache inside `bob ref scan` so a full writing scan does not re-plan PDFs whose bytes (and relevant ref-note state) are unchanged since their last successful plan. Today every full scan plans every library PDF; on the Mac that costs 78-307 s per run.

`bob tick`'s refs change gate (epic bob-cli-nb, src/native/tick/gates.rs) now skips whole scans when the lib/ and xlib/ listing fingerprint is unchanged, but it still forces a full scan at least every 6 hours and on any single file change, and then re-plans the entire library. A per-PDF cache (keyed by path, size, mtime, and the note-side inputs the planner reads) would make those scans proportional to what changed. The cache must not weaken the bob-cli-9c.1 guarantee that vault-sync never pushes a library PDF without its ref note, and must invalidate on parser or renderer version changes.

Proposed by bob-cli-nb.5 note #4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), recorded by the bob-cli-nb land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The bob-cli-nb epic owned only the orchestrator and its coarse listing-fingerprint gate; changing how bob ref scan plans individual PDFs is a separate highlights_ref performance change with its own correctness constraints.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-nb.5 proposed this follow-up: the tick refs gate skips unchanged libraries, but any scan that does run still re-plans every PDF for minutes.

payload.description: Narrowed the writing scan's bob_sync.lock window in the same scan_library/planning path a per-PDF cache would change
